results.title: All unauthorised billboards in Accra to be removed on November 14
results.content: State authorities and industry leaders have issued a final ultimatum to media agencies and property owners across the capital: clearly brand your outdoor advertising structures within seven days or see them dismantled in a massive joint enforcement sweep scheduled for November 14, 2026.

results.title: Over 53, 000 teenagers pregnant in 7 months – Advocates raise alarm
results.content: A total of 53,415 adolescent girls in the country became pregnant in the first half of 2026, according to data released by the Ghana Health Service (GHS).

results.content: A family’s fear of losing its sons to military conscription in the Ottoman Empire set in motion a journey that would eventually produce one of Ghana’s longstanding automotive businesses, Japan Motors Trading Company.

results.content: The Ghana Police Service has urged motorists and vehicle owners to verify traffic violation notices issued under the TraffiTech-GH automated enforcement system before paying, to avoid falling victim to fraud.

results.title: Australia’s oldest department store, David Jones, folds after 188 years
results.content: David Jones, Australia's oldest department store chain, has gone into voluntary administration, putting thousands of jobs at risk.

results.title: Firms told to publish salaries in job adverts ahead of new law
results.content: Businesses should publish salaries in job adverts now, Prime Minister Andy Burnham is telling firms, rather than wait for a new law to come in that will force them to do so.

results.title: Second buyer makes rescue bid for Poundland as retailer faces collapse
results.content: A second buyer has made a rescue bid for Poundland as the discount retailer teeters on the brink of collapse, with thousands of jobs at risk.

results.title: Ghana and Australia strengthen ties to push for Africa’s permanent UN Security Council seat
results.content: Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa says Ghana is forging closer ties with international allies to advance Africa’s call for reforms at the United Nations, particularly its demand for permanent representation on the UN Security Council.

results.title: Samia and Sekou Nkrumah reveal how the 1966 Coup affected their late brother
results.content: Samia and Sekou Nkrumah have recounted how the 1966 coup that toppled their father, Ghana’s first President, Dr Kwame Nkrumah, deeply affected their late brother, Gamel Nkrumah. The two siblings shared aspects of Gamel’s life and the difficulties he experienced following the overthrow of the Nkrumah government, including the family’s years in exile and his struggles after returning to Ghana. Gamel, who spent much of his life in Egypt, was among the children of Dr Kwame Nkrumah who returned to Ghana with the family in 1975 after the government of the then Head of State, General Ignatius Kutu Acheampong, facilitated their return from exile.

results.title: CPP Elders visit Nkrumah family to console them over death of Gamel Nkrumah
results.content: A delegation from the Convention People's Party (CPP), led by Comrade Chris Ziga, has visited the family of Ghana's first President, Dr Kwame Nkrumah, to express condolences following the death of his second son, Gamel Nkrumah. The delegation comprised members of the party's Council of Elders and National Working Committee. Receiving the delegation, Madam Samia Nkrumah and Sekou Nkrumah expressed sadness over the loss of their brother, who spent much of his life in Egypt. The family recounted how Gamel's life was shaped by the 1966 coup that toppled their father's government and forced them into exile. They said that although the family was formally invited back to Ghana by the Acheampong government in 1975, Gamel's return was short-lived.

results.title: A bitter end for Ronaldo – the icon who transformed Portugal
results.content: Cristiano Ronaldo's old rival Leo Messi left Argentina less than a month ago with a nation applauding him.

results.title: Kwadaso Agric College students turn ideas into market-ready agribusiness under CB-VET Ghana project
results.content: Innovation, entrepreneurship and practical skills are increasingly becoming the foundation of modern Agricultural Technical and Vocational Education and Training (ATVET) in Ghana, a shift clearly demonstrated by the CB-VET Ghana Project.

results.title: Ghana, Trinidad and Tobago explore new investments, expanded oil and gas partnerships
results.content: Ghana and Trinidad and Tobago are seeking to deepen their economic relations, with fresh discussions focusing on attracting new investments and expanding cooperation in the oil and gas sector.

results.title: I’m surprised I haven’t won TGMA Rapper of the Year – Teephlow

results.title: Build competence before seeking transformation – Dzigbordi Kwaku-Dosoo at TrueLife Experience
results.content: Keynote speaker Dzigbordi Kwaku-Dosoo has urged participants at the 2026 TrueLife Experience to move beyond drawing inspiration from others and develop the competence needed to inspire and influence people through their own work. Speaking at the event at the Kempinski Hotel in Accra, she highlighted the importance of building human competence, particularly in critical thinking, communication, public speaking and relationship-building. “You have to build the competence before you transform,” she said.

results.title: I built a $70m business while battling depression – Nekeya Parks at TrueLife Experience
results.content: Mindset mentor Nekeya Parks has revealed that she built a $70 million business while battling depression, urging people to identify and pursue what she described as their God-given purpose. Speaking at the 2026 TrueLife Experience at the Kempinski Hotel in Accra, she challenged participants to reflect on the ambitions they had before societal expectations and personal fears influenced their choices. "When you think about the dream that you had when you were smaller, when you were younger, before the world got its hands on you, before all the reasons why it felt too big landed, what was your original dream?" she asked. Ms Parks said many people were raised to pursue conventional career paths such as engineering, medicine and law because they were considered secure and financially rewarding.

results.title: Sir Sam Jonah shares life lessons on courage, humility and character at TrueLife Experience
results.content: Business leader Sir Sam Jonah has recounted how his upbringing in the mining town of Obuasi shaped his understanding of inequality, humility and respect for others. Speaking at the 2026 TrueLife Experience at the Kempinski Hotel in Accra on November 5, he reflected on the social and economic inequalities he observed growing up in the mining community. Held under the theme “The Audacity to Dare”, the two-day event brought together business executives, entrepreneurs, policymakers, professionals and emerging leaders to discuss personal development, leadership and purposeful action. Sir Sam Jonah said although wealth was being generated through gold mining in Obuasi, he observed that the people undertaking some of the hardest work did not necessarily have a corresponding say in how that wealth was managed.

results.title: ‘The Audacity to Dare’: TrueLife Experience challenges Ghanaians to pursue their ambitions
results.content: The 2026 TrueLife Experience has challenged Ghanaians to overcome fear, self-doubt and other personal limitations and take deliberate steps towards achieving their ambitions. Held under the theme “The Audacity to Dare”, the two-day event is taking place at the Kempinski Hotel in Accra on November 5 and 6. The gathering brings together business executives, entrepreneurs, policymakers, professionals and emerging leaders to discuss how courage, personal development and purposeful action can help individuals translate their potential into tangible results. Convener of the initiative, Dedo Kofi, said the programme uses real-life experiences to inspire participants and provide practical lessons they can apply in their personal and professional lives. “I wanted a conference that is very relatable to people. And I believe that stories are one of the ways people can easily relate,” she said.

results.title: UCAES SRC president urges young people to embrace agriculture
results.content: The newly elected President of the Students' Representative Council (SRC) of the University College of Agriculture and Environmental Studies (UCAES), Prince Amoako Atta, has called for increased youth participation in agriculture and environmental protection.

results.title: Prisons Service calls for national policy to support ex-convicts’ reintegration
results.content: The Ghana Prisons Service has called for a comprehensive National Reintegration Policy to address the stigma, discrimination and unemployment confronting formerly incarcerated persons as they seek to rebuild their lives after prison.

results.title: Ghanaians hold on to cherished food traditions as Christmas approaches
results.content: As Christmas approaches, families are preparing to celebrate the festive season with meals that bring them together and keep cherished food traditions alive. For many households, Christmas is not just about the celebrations but also the special dishes that have become part of their family traditions. Yet, with the cost of food and festive preparations often a concern, some families are finding ways to maintain their favourite meals without giving up what makes the season special. Speaking in a Christmas series exploring the foods families cannot do without during the festive season, Daniel Thompson said his family would continue preparing eba, describing it as an affordable meal. He said the family might switch from yellow gari to white gari to manage costs, but eba would remain part of their Christmas menu.

results.title: Ayariga urges residents to keep surroundings clean as AMA deploys 20 tricycles
results.content: The Minister for Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs, Mahama Ayariga, has urged residents to take greater responsibility for sanitation by ensuring waste is properly disposed of rather than leaving refuse outside their homes for government authorities to collect. He said keeping communities clean should go beyond maintaining individual homes to include the surrounding environment, stressing that sanitation was a shared responsibility. “Sometimes people clean their home and just put the waste right in front, and then they make it the responsibility of government to come and take the waste right in front of their homes,” he said.
